title: A Vancouver brunch weekend
summary: Shakshuka in Kitsilano, coffee on West 4th and a walk by the water, with choices for rain, lighter meals and a budget for two.

sections.heading: Choose an area, then a meal
sections.content: Choose Kitsilano for shakshuka, sourdough and the waterfront; Main Street or West 4th for browsing. Mount Pleasant can suit tofu scramble; the West End can suit pancakes. Yoghurt and granola work for a lighter meal. Combine one meal, one coffee and one walk rather than trying every idea. Check current menus, seating and reservation options first.

sections.heading: Ask before ordering
sections.content: For shakshuka, ask about eggs, spice and extra bread. For pancakes, compare portions and separate charges for berries, syrup or coffee; ask before sharing. Confirm milk, butter and stock even with a tofu scramble, and check access with the venue. In rain, a croissant and tea around Main Street can replace an uncovered queue.

sections.heading: A budget for two
sections.content: Add meals, drinks and extras before tax and your chosen tip. A rough sixty-to-ninety Canadian dollar allowance for two can be adjusted against the current menu. Transport and parking are separate; an allowance is not a tax rate. The eggs Benedict menu price may be only part of the bill.

sources.title: Eggs Benedict and the rest of the bill

sections.heading: A walk and a considerate coffee stop
sections.content: Take a breakfast sandwich toward False Creek or Kitsilano for roughly half an hour to an hour, shortening the walk when needed. Take rubbish away, leave wildlife alone and avoid slippery edges. At a West 4th café, ask about laptops and power, release a small table when queues grow and take calls outside. Bad weather is a reason to shorten the day; tea and a croissant can be enough.
